The drone-based sprint profiling system employs a multi-stage pipeline: first, YOLOv8s tracks athlete positions via aerial video; second, perspective transformation maps pixel coordinates to real-world meters; third, velocity is derived from time-position data using exponential saturation model v(t) = v_max(1 - e^(-t/τ)); fourth, force and ratio are computed via Newtonian dynamics and vector decomposition; finally, F0, V0, and SFV are derived from these core parameters. The system demonstrates strong reliability (ICC ≥ 0.59) for Vmax and related metrics, but shows significant bias in early-acceleration parameters such as Amax and F0 due to tracking instability. This failure mode arises from insufficient resolution during initial acceleration, where small tracking errors propagate into large deviations in derived metrics. The model's breakdown occurs at low velocities where sensor noise dominates signal fidelity. In contrast, late-phase metrics like Pmax and split times show minimal bias and high consistency, indicating robustness in steady-state velocity regimes. The dual nature of the system—reliability in top-speed phase but instability in acceleration—reflects a fundamental trade-off between temporal resolution and spatial accuracy in drone-based motion capture.
